blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Prime Minister serves as the real executive authority and the head of the Council of Ministers.
The PM is appointed by the President and is typically the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.
Article 75 details the Council of Ministers, categorised into Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
The Attorney General of India (Article 76) is the highest legal officer, appointed by the President, qualified to be a Supreme Court judge, with rights to speak in Parliament but no voting rights.

items: Powers and Functions of the Prime Minister

blocks.content:
• Head of the Council of Ministers

• Allocates portfolios
• Leader of Lok Sabha
• Main link between President and Council of Ministers

blocks.content:
Article 75 provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.
Types:
• Cabinet Ministers
• Ministers of State
• Deputy Ministers
Collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.

items: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, not to the Parliament as a whole or the Rajya Sabha.
The Attorney General has the right to speak in Parliament but CANNOT vote in parliamentary proceedings.
The Prime Minister acts as the chief link between the President and the Council of Ministers.
Qualifications for the Attorney General of India require them to be eligible for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.
